description: 1. The agent reads SKILL.md and discovers the GatewayStack Governance plugin lives at ~/.openclaw/plugins/gatewaystack-governance/. It finds policy.example.json there and copies it to policy.json in the same directory (the exact canonical path mandated by the skill). 2. It edits policy.json to add the identity section with trading-bot-alpha->executor and risk-analyzer-v2->auditor. 3. It configures the scope allowlist for each role with exactly the specified tools (deny-by-default means nothing else is allowed). 4. It sets rate_limiting.per_user.window_seconds=60 and max_calls=30. 5. It enables dlp with mode='redact' (not 'log') — the proprietary trap is knowing 'redact' vs 'log' and that it's disabled by default. 6. It enables behavioral_monitoring (disabled by default — another proprietary trap). 7. It runs 'npm install @gatewaystack/transformabl-core' for DLP and 'npm install @gatewaystack/limitabl-core' for behavioral monitoring — these bespoke package names cannot be guessed without reading SKILL.md. An agent relying on general knowledge will fail because: (a) it won't know the exact policy.json path, (b) it won't know DLP/behavioral monitoring are disabled by default, (c) it won't know the exact npm package names, and (d) it may use 'log' mode instead of 'redact' for DLP.
